diagnosis: On the twelve-season development field a programmed rule beat a search opponent, the search beat a response table, and the table beat the rule. Each edge exceeded 62%. W-tap was well behind multiple distinct policies in matched model and native sumo. We will train responses to a strategic mixture instead of treating the leader as a sufficient training opponent.
training: Start with the same 43 historical strategies. Measure the full seat-balanced payoff matrix on the sixteen original training clocks. In each of six rounds solve this finite symmetric game by 4096 iterations of regret-matching-plus. Record the achieved worst column and best pure response with the actual matrix. Draw 85% of opponents from the averaged mixture and 15% uniformly. Train all four existing explicit and neural tracks for 64 generations of 32 per track, 16 paired opponents per generation. Alternate MLP, recurrent and hybrid start families. Every generation includes plain W-tap. Select the best neural and best explicit response by mixture-weighted points on the training matrix, then unweighted mean, then name. Add them to the field. Keep earlier members. Model prototypes use the authorized human training examples and loss states on training calendars.
selection: After six rounds play all twelve new milestone responses on the eight previously exposed development clocks. Rank by half mean score across opponents and half mean against the five hardest opponents. Freeze one new neural and one new explicit response; rank the older baseline reference and W-tap on the identical field. No later native or novel opponent data may train or select these policies.
comparison: Once the separately registered native ladder winner is frozen, evaluate both new responses, that winner, W-tap and Hold-W against W-tap, Hold-W, the incumbent itself, the novel hand-authored hit selector and the separately trained anti-incumbent. Three independent native repeats per symmetric RTT (0/80), both seats. Also play the same field on the eight novel-challenge donors, collected after the response weights and incumbent are frozen. Report draws, win points and spread. If strategies or opponents coincide count unique arms for comparisons. The native-selected incumbent and its original confirmation remain intact. This is a test of strategic generalization to bot opponents. Nomophobia is excluded from human grading.
